channel.title: Defense News
channel.description: Timely, source-attributed coverage of global military developments, defense technology, and international security.

item.title: South Korea Tests First Homegrown Hypersonic Glide Vehicle
item.description: South Korea conducted its first successful flight test of a domestically developed hypersonic boost-glide vehicle on Oct. 8, with President Lee Jae Myung observing, marking the country's entry into a hypersonic arms race on the Korean Peninsula.

item.title: Houthi Missile Strike on Riyadh Airport Kills 12, Wounds 309
item.description: A missile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Oct. 10, killing at least 12 and wounding 309 in Saudi Arabia's deadliest attack in more than a decade, as President Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis.

item.title: Coast Guard Orders Its First MQ-9B Drones in $248 Million Deal
item.description: The U.S. Coast Guard has placed a $248 million order for its first MQ-9B drones to extend its maritime surveillance reach.

item.title: Lockheed Unveils PAC-3 Edge, Its Next-Generation Patriot Interceptor
item.description: Lockheed Martin has unveiled the PAC-3 Edge, a next-generation Patriot interceptor backed by hundreds of millions in company investment.

item.title: B-52 to Get Stealthy LRASM Anti-Ship Missiles, Completing the Bomber Trio
item.description: The B-52 is being integrated with the stealthy AGM-158C LRASM, giving all three U.S. bombers a long-range anti-ship punch.

item.title: GDLS to Deliver New PERCH 2.0 Loitering Munition Prototypes to Army This Month
item.description: General Dynamics Land Systems will deliver four PERCH 2.0 loitering munition prototypes to the Army's 1st Cavalry Division by the end of October.

item.title: New Leaders, New Drone Command: What to Expect from AUSA 2026
item.description: The Army's autonomy push and the fate of its modernization programs will dominate this year's AUSA conference, with new leaders and a new drone command in the spotlight.

item.title: Sweden Launches First Patriot Air Defense Mission to Poland
item.description: Sweden has launched its first Patriot air defense mission to Poland as part of a NATO operation, amid a heated domestic security debate.

item.title: Hanwha Eyes Army's Tracked Howitzer Program After Wheeled-Arty Win
item.description: Hanwha plans to offer its K9 tracked howitzers for the Army's next artillery competition after winning the wheeled howitzer contest.

item.title: Zero Trust Gets Harder as Every Weapon and AI Agent Needs an Identity
item.description: The Pentagon's Zero Trust push is entering a harder phase: giving every user, device, weapon system, and AI agent its own verifiable identity.

item.title: Australia Receives Second HIMARS Tranche Two Years Ahead of Schedule
item.description: The Australian Army has received a second tranche of U.S.-built HIMARS rocket launchers, arriving two years ahead of schedule.

item.title: Arizona Desert Drone Tests Offer Hard Lessons for CENTCOM's Counter-UAS Fight
item.description: Counter-drone experiments in the Arizona desert are shaping how U.S. forces in the Middle East confront the drone threat.

item.title: Pentagon, Lockheed Weigh Multi-Year F-35 Production and Sustainment Deal
item.description: The Pentagon and Lockheed Martin are negotiating a multi-year F-35 production and sustainment agreement, though doubts remain over long-term cost savings.

item.title: Pentagon, Raytheon Sign Up to $6.3 Billion Multi-Year Deal for SM-3 IB Missiles
item.description: The Pentagon and Raytheon have signed a multi-year contract worth up to $6.3 billion for SM-3 Block IB interceptors, months after a framework deal to raise production.

item.title: U.S. Pitches F-35 as Portugal Weighs Replacing Its F-16s
item.description: Washington is making a hard push for the F-35 as Portugal decides what will replace its aging F-16 fleet.

item.title: Navy Doubles Down on X-BAT VTOL 'Fighter' Drone
item.description: The Navy is accelerating the X-BAT, an ambitious vertical-takeoff drone meant to bring fighter-like capability to ships without catapults.

item.title: Army Shows 'Blackbeard' Hypersonic Missile Firing from Ground Launcher
item.description: The Army has shown its Blackbeard hypersonic missile firing from a mobile ground launcher, part of a push for cheaper, more mobile hypersonic weapons.

item.title: Could Germany Join GCAP? UK Seeks to Advance Potential Fighter Switch
item.description: Britain is pushing to advance talks on Germany potentially joining the GCAP sixth-generation fighter program after the collapse of FCAS.

item.title: Where the Carriers Are: Bush Takes Liberty in Phuket, Washington Covers Iran
item.description: USS George H.W. Bush pulled into Phuket after 188 days at sea, leaving USS George Washington as the sole carrier facing Iran.

item.title: Anduril and U.S. Navy Announce $6.6 Billion Push to Expand Submarine Industrial Base
item.description: Anduril Industries and the U.S. Navy are investing a combined $6.6 billion to expand America's submarine industrial base, anchored by a new software-defined shipyard.

item.title: First F-16 Block 72 Takes Flight, Seven Years After Morocco's Order
item.description: The first F-16 Block 72 — the Pratt & Whitney-powered Viper ordered by Morocco seven years ago — has finally flown.

item.title: Texas Guard's AH-64E Apaches Relocate to JBSA-Lackland in Army Reshuffle
item.description: The Texas Guard's Apache attack battalion has begun moving to Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland under an Army restructuring plan.

item.title: USAF's New HACM Hypersonic Cruise Missile Makes First Release Over Australian Range
item.description: The U.S. Air Force has carried out the first release of its Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile over an Australian test range, a milestone after major program delays.

item.title: Navy Commissions Destroyer USS Ted Stevens in Alaska Ceremony
item.description: The Navy has commissioned its newest destroyer, USS Ted Stevens, into active service during a ceremony in Whittier, Alaska.

item.title: B-1B Bombers Beat a Hasty Retreat from England Amid Iran Threats
item.description: B-1B bombers have abruptly left RAF Fairford in England after Iran openly threatened the base that hosted them during Operation Epic Fury.

item.title: Northrop Grumman's Talon Blue Drone Takes Flight in CCA Race
item.description: Northrop Grumman's Talon Blue has flown, staking its claim in the Air Force's Collaborative Combat Aircraft competition.

item.title: One Navy Squadron's Staggering Weapons Bill from the War with Iran
item.description: A single Navy fighter squadron — VFA-41 — expended hundreds of air-to-air and air-to-surface weapons during Operation Epic Fury against Iran.

item.title: Germany Finally Gives Its F125 Frigates Real Teeth with IRIS-T Missiles
item.description: Germany is arming its 7,200-ton F125 frigates with IRIS-T SLM surface-to-air missiles, addressing their notoriously light armament.

item.title: Taiwan's First F-16 Block 70 Fighters Finally Arrive
item.description: Taiwan has taken delivery of its first two new F-16 Block 70 fighters, kicking off a long-awaited fleet expansion as pressure from mainland China grows.

item.title: Secretive AIM-260 Missile Spotted on Australian Super Hornet
item.description: The long-range AIM-260 air-to-air missile has been photographed on an Australian F/A-18F Super Hornet, promising a major reach boost against Chinese threats.
